chunks: Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Ali al-Tamimi. He said: My master Ali b. Musa al-Ridha (AS) narrated to me from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them) from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family),

that he said: Whoever would be gladdened to look upon the red rod that Allah planted with His hand — and to be of those who hold fast to it — should take Ali and the Imams from his descendants as their guardian; for they are the choicest of Allah (Almighty and Majestic) and His elite; and they are the Immaculate (ma'sumun), free from every sin and error.

key_terms.الْقَضِيبُ الْأَحْمَرُ: The 'red rod/branch' — a metaphorical image symbolizing divine authority and the covenant of wilayah, planted by Allah Himself, evoking both the rod of Moses and Quranic imagery of divine planting.
key_terms.الْمَعْصُومُونَ: 'Ismah (infallibility/immaculateness) — the doctrinal concept that the Imams and the Prophet are divinely protected from sin and error; here explicitly applied to Ali and the Imams.
key_terms.خِيَرَةُ اللَّهِ: The choicest/elect of Allah — a Quranic expression (cf. 28:68) indicating divine election and distinction from ordinary people.
key_terms.صَفْوَتُهُ: The pure distillate / elite — the cream of creation, those most refined in character and chosen by divine selection.
key_terms.فَلْيَتَوَلَّ: From tawalla — to take as one's wali (guardian/master); accepting the wilayah (guardianship) of the Imam in the theological Shia sense.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the 'red rod planted by Allah's hand' teach about Imamate and infallibility in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq, transmitted through an unbroken chain from Imam al-Ridha back through the Imams to the Prophet (SAWA), uses the powerful metaphor of the 'red rod' — a divine standard planted by Allah's own hand — to signify wilayah (guardianship) over the Ahl al-Bayt. The Prophet enjoins walayah over Ali and the twelve Imams from his lineage, affirming their status as Allah's choicest elect and their essential quality of 'ismah (infallibility) from all sin and error. This teaching would have resonated powerfully with the early Shia community as a comprehensive statement of Imamology: the Imams are not merely worthy leaders but divinely planted, infallible guideposts.
